newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up again on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up again on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks continued a three-day rally rising with U.S. stocks on sustained foreign interest, although some traders saw the surge slowing in coming sessions on profit-taking.
"The trend is definitely up, but we could see an adjustment soon," said Multinvest broker Reinaldo Uribe.
However, analysts said market strength was underpinned by institutional "buy and hold forever" investors.
"These investors are looking for bellwether exposure to the market and don't seem to be that interested in price," said InvestAnalysis consultant Alex Dalmady in a commentary.

"In 1996, it was the momentum players and the daring. The smart money," Dalmady said. "This year it is the long-term money ... (with) large-cap, high-profile stocks grabbing more than their usual share of the action."
Telephone company CANTV once again led gainers, closing up 119.00 bolivars at 2,500.00, as a total of 87 million shares, worth six billion bolivars ($12.6 million), traded in the session.
The bolsa's 19-share index climbed 0.25 percent to close at 6,627.80 points, while Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, rose 1.43 percent to end at 105.84 points.
Among traded issues, 15 rose, 15 fell and ten closed flat.
